unresolved_candidates.reason: The target says the person who turns away from the law has himself abhorred his own prayer. It is not rewritten as God declaring the prayer an abomination; that proposed direct equivalence to the prayer becoming sin remains pending.

Daniel explicitly refrains from anointing with oil and loses strength when he sees the vision. Psalm108 says the flesh was altered because of oil, not for lack of oil, and ties weakened knees to fasting. A direct equation of those causal details is not established.

Psalm3 names the Lord as the speaker's helper and head-lifter, but does not contain the torrent, drinking on a journey or the consequent head-lifting. The proposed specific restoration or victory interpretation of the whole source image remains unestablished.

Psalm28 says Lebanon is ground fine like the calf and the beloved like a young one-horned animal. It does not describe leaping mountains; a familiar skipping-Lebanon rendering cannot be substituted for the actual target.
Jeremiah promises purification for the souls of those who walk the good way. It does not say rest for your souls in this edition, so the proposed direct rest formula is not counted.
Paul explicitly identifies the blessed cup with participation in Christ's blood. The psalm names a cup of salvation without that identification, so an asserted identity of the cups is left pending.

The Gospel places Hosanna beside the explicit quotation of Psalm117:26, but it does not render Hosanna as Save now in the supplied English text. An exact lexical identification for source117:25 has not been independently checked and receives no credit.

The entry narrative contains branches and the neighboring psalm's blessing, but it does not mention the altar horns or identify its procession as this festival. The proposed specific event identification remains pending despite the supported separate comparison with Leviticus' festival boughs.
